blocks.text: About this page

A sub-processor is a company we pay to handle personal data for us, on our instructions. This page lists our sub-processors, the other places your data can go when you use {company.name}, and where our servers are. It covers our website and all our products. We add a provider here before it starts handling personal data for us.

Our [Privacy Policy](/instant/legal/privacy) explains how we use personal data. When business customers of the API, our Enterprise services or the Assistant Bot give us personal data to process, our [Data Processing Addendum](/instant/legal/dpa) applies.

blocks.text: If you use a local AI model on your Mac, your conversation goes to that model instead of an AI provider. Questions the agents send to {company.name} cloud research still go to our cloud and to the providers above.
We have no payment provider, no analytics service and no advertising network. We do not sell personal data.
Where our servers are

We host our cloud services and databases on Google Cloud in the EU, in the Netherlands (region europe-west4). This includes the website, the web app, the service the Desktop App talks to, the API and its own database, and the files and reports your agents store in the cloud. Each Enterprise project is hosted in an EU Google Cloud region we agree with the customer.
Some providers, such as Clerk and Google Gemini, may process data in the US or elsewhere. Data is encrypted in transit (HTTPS), and our cloud provider encrypts it at rest.
Transfers outside the EU

When personal data leaves the EEA, the UK or Switzerland, the law requires a safeguard. For Clerk, the safeguard is the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, with the EU Standard Contractual Clauses as a fallback (GDPR Art. 45 and 46). With Google Cloud, your data is hosted in the EU.
For Google Gemini, we use Google's paid service. Google's paid-service terms and its data processing terms apply to the data we send.
To get a copy of the safeguards that apply to your data, write to {company.privacyEmail}.
Foreign government requests

EU law asks cloud providers to say where their infrastructure is and what they do about requests from governments outside the EU (EU Data Act, Art. 28). This applies to all data, not only personal data.

items: Our infrastructure: our cloud services and databases run on Google Cloud in the Netherlands, under EU law. Sign-in runs on Clerk in the United States.
Google and Clerk are US companies or part of US groups, so US law can apply to them as well.
If a government or court outside the EU asks us for your data, we check whether the request is lawful and whether EU or national law allows us to answer it.
Where we can, we object to requests that are unlawful or too broad. We hand over only the minimum the request lawfully requires.
We tell the customer concerned before we answer, unless the law forbids it.

blocks.text: US state privacy laws

Under US state privacy laws, Google Cloud, Clerk and Cloudflare work for us as service providers or processors. Google's terms set how Google may use data we send to the Gemini API, as explained in [How Our AI Works](/instant/legal/ai#data-models-see). We do not sell personal data or share it for targeted advertising.
Changes to this list
When we add or replace a sub-processor, we update this page and the date at the top.
Business customers covered by our [Data Processing Addendum](/instant/legal/dpa) get notice before a new sub-processor starts handling their data. They can object, as the addendum sets out.
